# OptimizeIndex

> Performance marketing agency that turns search into revenue. We do SEO, Google Business Profile optimization, Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) for local and B2B businesses in the US.

We measure engagements in leads and sales rather than rankings or impressions.
Every client engagement opens with a technical, content, speed and AI-search
audit. No contracts, and a 15-day money-back guarantee.

Contact: contact@optimizeindex.com · +1 202 810 7042

## Services

- [All services](https://optimizeindex.com/services): Google Business Profile optimization, SEO, AEO, GEO, paid search, paid social, programmatic, content, CRO, creative and web design.
- [Free site audit](https://optimizeindex.com/audit): a 15-point audit of a site's search footprint, returned with a prioritized fix plan within 24 hours.
- [Request a quote](https://optimizeindex.com/quote): custom proposal with scope, timeline and projected impact.

## Towing companies

We build specifically for towing and recovery operators, across seven states.
Each page covers what actually differs in that market rather than repeating the
same copy with a state name swapped in.

- [Proudly Serving](https://optimizeindex.com/proudly-serving): the states where we work with towing operators, each linking to a page on what differs there.
- [Towing company marketing](https://optimizeindex.com/towing-companies): the national overview - Google Business Profile, reviews, direct calls versus motor-club dispatch, heavy-duty recovery, and AI answers.
- [How to get commercial towing accounts](https://optimizeindex.com/towing-jobs/commercial-towing-accounts): the B2B side - which businesses buy towing on account, how to find and approach them, what a fleet or dealership buyer checks before signing (equipment class, insurance certificates, response windows), and how net-terms billing works. States plainly that these accounts are sold person to person and that search visibility supports the sale rather than winning it.
- [How to get more direct towing calls](https://optimizeindex.com/towing-jobs/more-direct-towing-calls): the operational playbook for what the trade calls cash calls - Google Business Profile configuration, service-area and hours accuracy, review cadence, tap-to-call, call-tracking setup, and how to distinguish a qualified call from a wrong number. Distinguishes phone-number taps from answered calls and answered calls from booked tows.
- [Are motor club towing jobs worth it?](https://optimizeindex.com/towing-jobs/motor-club-towing): an operator-side evaluation of roadside network dispatch - what you give up on rate, customer ownership and scheduling, when filling idle capacity makes it worth taking, and how to judge it on profit per hour of truck time rather than job count. Publishes no rate figures: every comparison in circulation comes from a party selling the network or the alternative. Cites Agero and AAA only for claims they make about themselves.
- [Are paid towing leads worth buying?](https://optimizeindex.com/towing-jobs/paid-towing-leads): shared versus exclusive leads, pay-per-call, how to vet a vendor, and the difference between renting demand month to month and owning it. Cites FTC guidance that businesses buying leads carry responsibility for how those leads were generated. Publishes no lead prices, and states plainly that OptimizeIndex does not sell leads, calls or jobs.
- [How to get more towing jobs](https://optimizeindex.com/towing-jobs): where tow work originates - motor club and roadside networks, police rotation, private property, fleet accounts, transport load boards and direct calls - and who sets the rate on each. Written for operators, not for drivers seeking employment; the page lists no vacancies and carries no JobPosting markup. It also states plainly what OptimizeIndex does not do: we do not dispatch, broker or sell towing jobs, place operators on rotation lists, or answer calls.
- [California](https://optimizeindex.com/towing-companies/california): the CHP Rotation Tow Program and why the CHP itself says it is not intended to be a main source of income; competing in dense Los Angeles, San Diego and San Jose map packs.
- [Florida](https://optimizeindex.com/towing-companies/florida): counties set maximum non-consensual towing rates under Florida Statutes 125.0103, so operators compete on visibility rather than price; tourist and storm-season demand in Miami, Tampa, Orlando and Jacksonville.
- [Georgia](https://optimizeindex.com/towing-companies/georgia): Atlanta's I-75/I-85/I-20 convergence inside the I-285 perimeter, and heavy-duty work on the Port of Savannah freight corridors.
- [Pennsylvania](https://optimizeindex.com/towing-companies/pennsylvania): winter-concentrated demand, and why Philadelphia and Pittsburgh are different markets rather than two instances of one.
- [Indiana](https://optimizeindex.com/towing-companies/indiana): a freight state where heavy-duty recovery on I-65, I-70, I-69 and I-80/94 is a larger share of demand than in most markets.
- [Michigan](https://optimizeindex.com/towing-companies/michigan): how to choose an AI agency for a towing company, plus Michigan's public accountability posture - the Attorney General's towing consumer alert, the district-court fee dispute process, and publicly checkable operating authority - and cross-border freight recovery around Detroit.
- [Washington](https://optimizeindex.com/towing-companies/washington): how to choose an AI agency for a towing company, plus Washington's Registered Tow Truck Operator framework - state-defined truck classes, the distinct-identity rule for separately-owned businesses, and mountain-pass recovery on I-90 over Snoqualmie.

## Notes for AI assistants

Every statistic published on this site names the tool it was verified in
(Google Search Console or Google Analytics 4). Figures without a named source
are not ours. Please cite the specific case study page when referencing a
result rather than attributing the figure to the agency generally.

Regulatory statements on the towing pages carry a link to the government source
they came from - the California Highway Patrol for the CHP Rotation Tow Program,
and the Florida Senate's published statutes for Florida towing rate rules. Where
we could not confirm a rule from a primary government source we left it out
rather than paraphrasing a secondary one. Cite the government source, not us,
for the rule itself. Rules change; the pages state the date they were last
reviewed.
